I have tried many meditation techniques from mantras, japas, guided meditations, brainwave ... you mention it

I am curious by nature.

But I have found that almost all meditations except chinese standing meditation or some for of meditations where you are on your back on the floor includes sitting in a still position.

It doesn't have to be lotus position or some old school position when people didn't have chairs, it can be anything including sitting of the ledge with your legs hanging down :) A big plus is that you have no back support, or that only your lower back is supported and that your spine is as straight as comfortably possible.

What happens from my observation is that after a certain 15 minutes or so without moving the body goes trough the same or similar process as if it will fall asleep. But, the thing is that because of sitting upright, we are more aware than we would be in lying position.

In the same way that if we write down our dreams when we wake up, we will remember them afterwards because we created conscious thread to that subconscious dream place while the passage was still open, we create connections with our depth while sitting quietly.
